evidence_items.publisher: OpenAI; copy hosted by Open Future
evidence_items.locator: Page 12, Training AI Models Does Not Violate Copyright Law

receipt.public_excerpt:
The factual metadata and fundamental information that AI models learn from training data are
not protected by copyright law.

evidence_items.explanation: The submission argues that training qualifies as fair use and that licensing every training work is impracticable. The quoted sentence supplies part of its stated legal rationale, establishing advocacy during 2023.

receipt.public_excerpt: Training AI models using publicly available internet materials is fair use

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI explicitly advocates fair-use protection for this training. This is evidence of its position, not a finding that its legal argument is correct.

evidence_items.locator: Page 10, Copyright: Promoting the Freedom to Learn

receipt.public_excerpt: Applying the fair use doctrine to AI is not only a matter of American competitiveness

evidence_items.explanation: The submission continues the fair-use argument and criticizes restrictions on access to training material. This establishes that the advocacy persisted into 2025.

receipt.public_excerpt: Axel Springer and OpenAI have announced a global partnership

evidence_items.explanation: The announcement describes publisher benefits and use of content for model training. It qualifies any suggestion that OpenAI rejected all partnerships or benefits for creators, while remaining compatible with its general fair-use position.
